newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Slough sees harder rental rates.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Slough sees harder rental rates.

text.p: Slough Estates, Britain's largest industrial property company, sees a continued hardening in prime rental rates in the current year after an increase of around five percent in 1996, chairman Sir Nigel Mobbs said on Thursday.
Mobbs said market conditions for development lettings were positive in the areas where Slough has most exposure, mainly the Thames Valley.
"Conditions will remain positive this and beyond this year," Mobbs told Reuters in an interview. "Our own predictions certainly go up to the end of the century."
Mobbs said he doubted that a change of government after Britain's May 1 election would have any significant impact on Slough's business.
"I don't think we will see changes at the customer level, whether it would have an impact on the investment side because of changes in taxation, only time will tell," Mobbs said.
He added that government actions would likely be dominated by the level of interest rates, adding he expected a rise in rates whichever party wins the election but only "a fairly modest increment."

Slough announced two further lettings in its Buchanan Galleries shopping centre development in Glasgow with 10 percent of the development being taken up by Next Plc and upmarket home furnishings store Habitat.
It said its development for express cargo and delivery company DHL near Brussels airport was continuing on schedule and would be completed in May.

Mobbs also said that Slough was still in discussions with Welwyn and Hatfield Council and the Department of the Environment on payment by the council of the 38 million stg awarded to Slough for fraudulent misrepresentation by the council in a court case last year.
